svg.text: Adaptive refinement: a quadtree standing in for the octree
Refinement is purely geometric — a cell is split if the surface may pass through it. No curvature, no error term.
118 leaves total, 44 of them at maxDepth carrying Hermite data.
A uniform grid at the same resolution would be 256 cells, all of them allocated.
buildNode: exactly three outcomes
depth >= maxDepth
sample 8 corner signs, populate the 12 edges,
allocate HermiteLeafData
depth < minDepth
force a split regardless of geometry —
defends against an L-shaped part whose root
centre sits in empty space
otherwise
split iff cellOverlaps(bounds), else become a
Hermite-less leaf with leaf.reset()
cellOverlaps — and the assumption it hides
For a mesh: a pure BVH/AABB descent, no field evaluation at all.
For a generic field: 8 corner signs, then a conservative test
|f(centre)| <= 0.5 * |cell diagonal|
which is only valid if |grad f| <= 1. A steeper field can hide a
bubble inside the cell — pruned, and the geometry vanishes.
Where the adaptivity actually comes from
Every surface-touching cell is refined to maxDepth. Variable
resolution is added afterwards by simplifyHermiteOctree,
where the QEF error is already available for free.
